Task: Improve the understandability of the test `SimpleBloomFilterTest_testMerge.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/commons-collections/manual/testcases/SimpleBloomFilterTest/SimpleBloomFilterTest_testMerge.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

I've read both files. The original test has a lot of dead helper code (and even a broken non-compiling declaration on line 47 with an undefined type `T`). For `testMerge`, only `getTestShape()`, `createEmptyFilter(...)`, and `createFilter(Shape, Hasher)` are actually exercised. Let me write a clean, understandable version that preserves the exact runtime behavior.`BadHasher` isn't on the classpath (it was an inherited test helper in the original's base class). The other helpers compiled fine. I'll define `BadHasher` as a local nested class reproducing the exact same behavior — a hasher whose sole index is the constructor value, which `merge` rejects when out of range.Compiles successfully (`COMPILE_OK`). The refactored `SimpleBloomFilterTest_testMerge` preserves the original test's exact runtime behavior while improving readability: dead/unused helpers and the broken non-compiling declaration were removed, the kept helpers and each merge scenario now have clear names and explanatory comments, and the previously-inherited `BadHasher` is now a small self-contained nested class with identical semantics.
